subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — per-token commit & displacement ask
messages:
From: Sarah Lang <sarah@dataforge.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataForge Procurement <procurement@dataforge.ai>
Date: 2026-01-22T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing + competitor displacement question

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood’s latency profile but pricing is the key gating factor for our contract. Our procurement and engineering teams are trying to compare total unit economics vs. the cloud vendor endpoints and Anthropic. Two specific asks:

1) Can you provide a per-token commit tier proposal (monthly committed tokens) with clear unit price at each tier?
2) If DataForge shows a lower invoice from a public vendor (e.g., OpenAI or Anthropic) for comparable usage, what does Redwood’s price-matching or displacement credit look like? We need the mechanics (proof, audit window, retro credits).

Scope: ~30M tokens/month initially, ramping to ~120M over 12 months.

Can you loop in legal/proc as needed — Cc’ing procurement.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lang
Head of Platform
DataForge.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-23T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing + competitor displacement question

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear asks. I’m looping Ben (pricing/sales) and Marissa (AM) into this thread. Quick note while we pull the detailed sheet: we routinely do commit-tier pricing for hosted API customers and have an explicit displacement policy, but the economics depend on term, minimums, and audit mechanics.

Ben — can you prepare a per-token tier sheet sized for their ramp (30M -> 120M) and include an example displacement clause (what counts as proof, lookback window, cap on retro credits)?

I’ll attach an initial draft MA for procurement to review once Ben confirms numbers.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lang <sarah@dataforge.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-27T09:44:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API pricing + competitor displacement question

Sarah / team —

Attached is a draft tier sheet (redwood-pricing-comparison.xlsx). Summary proposal (high level):

- Month-to-month list: $0.00065 / token (base public hosted)
- 3-month commit (>= 25M/mo): $0.00050 / token
- 6-month commit (>= 50M/mo): $0.00040 / token
- 12-month commit (>= 100M/mo): $0.00030 / token

Example effective math: if you commit 100M tokens / mo at $0.00030, that’s $30,000 / mo. Compared to a public vendor effective rate of $0.00035, the delta is $5,000 / mo.

Displacement / price-match proposal (draft):
- If DataForge provides an invoice from a public vendor with line-item usage for a directly comparable API (same model class, comparable latency/throughput), Redwood will:
  - Evaluate the invoice within 15 business days.
  - If validated, Redwood will provide retroactive credits to match the verified per-token price for the covered period, limited to the difference between our invoiced amount and the verified vendor amount, capped at the committed monthly spend for the affected month.
  - Auditable proof: vendor invoice + aggregate usage logs + sample request/response hashes (to show same model class/payload shape).

Limits and conditions:
- Price-match requires at least a 3-month committed term; cannot be applied to month-to-month list rates.
- Maximum retro credit window: 90 days after invoice date.
- One price-match event per rolling 12 months for the same account unless negotiated.

I can tighten language for procurement/legal if helpful.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Lang <sarah@dataforge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataForge Procurement <procurement@dataforge.ai>
Date: 2026-01-29T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API pricing + competitor displacement question

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and our engineering lead:

1) For displacement, can you demonstrate example math against Anthropic’s recent public pricing? For instance: Anthropic invoice shows 90M tokens at $0.00028 => $25,200. If Redwood’s committed rate for that month would have been $0.00030 => $27,000, we expect a $1,800 credit. Please confirm you’d honor the per-token delta in that simple case.

2) We need an SLA/latency parity statement in the MA. If you’re matching price we also need operational alignment (same or measurable SLA).

3) Procurement asks for a 60-day lookback window (not 90), and the ability to request one independent third-party audit per year for validation.

We’re also interested in a pilot discount for the first 3 months if we go with a 12-month commit — helps us justify the vendor switch internally.

Appreciate quick turn — procurement would like a redline-ready MA.

—Sarah
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lang <sarah@dataforge.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-03T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API pricing + competitor displacement question

Sarah —

Quick replies inline:  

1) Math example: yes, we would credit the per-token delta as you outlined (Anthropic example). Our commercial team suggested 60 days is reasonable; operationally we prefer 90 for evidence collection but we can accept 60 if DataForge provides timely vendor invoices & logs.

2) SLA: we’ll include a route-specific SLO table in the MA (p99 latency targets by model family, uptime SLA for hosted endpoints). If SLA breaches are validated, credits follow the standard SLA credit schedule.

3) Pilot: we can offer a 25% off per-token rate for the first 3 months on top of a 12-month commit for accounts that hit >= 75M tokens/mo by month 4. Alternatively, we can offer $X in onboarding credits if you prefer a lower time-based threshold.

Proc notes: internal approval required for onboarding credit > $50k — happy to surface that once we have the committed tiers.

I’ll prepare a redline of the MA with the displacement language and SLA section and share a DocuSign-ready copy. Attaching DF_MA_proposal_v2 (draft).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lang <sarah@dataforge.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-02-08T10:31:00-08:00
Subject: Updated proposal + displacement language (DF-2026-058)

Team —

We put together an updated commit proposal and tightened displacement language per the asks. Highlights:  

- 12-month commit (100M tokens/mo): $0.00028 / token for months 1–3, then $0.00030 / token for months 4–12. (This gives an aggressive ramp incentive and covers pilot.)
- Displacement: 60-day lookback accepted. Retro credit equals the per-token delta, capped at committed monthly spend. One self-initiated third-party audit / year allowed; Redwood covers administrative review costs up to $5k.
- SLA: p99 latency targets and uptime 99.9% across hosted endpoints for committed routes. SLA credits apply independently of price-match credits.

We’ve attached a DocuSign-ready MA (DataForge_MA_proposal_v2.pdf) and the pricing workbook. If DataForge signs the MA with these terms we’ll also include a one-time onboarding credit of $25k to ease migration costs.

Next steps: Sarah/procurement — please confirm acceptance of the displacement mechanics and we’ll send the DocuSign URL.

Thanks,
Vivek
From: Sarah Lang <sarah@dataforge.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: DataForge Procurement <procurement@dataforge.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Updated proposal + displacement language (DF-2026-058)

Vivek / Marissa —

Thanks — that layout addresses most of our concerns. Procurement is comfortable with the 60-day lookback and the audit language as long as the MA includes: (a) explicit list of acceptable evidence (invoice + per-route usage + sample payloads), and (b) the cap mechanics called out.

One small ask on the onboarding credit: can the $25k be applied as a first-month invoice credit rather than an offset to fees in month 6? That improves our vendor transition cashflow.

If you can update the MA language to those two points and send the DocuSign link, I’ll route to legal and procurement for signature.

Assuming the small edits, DataForge intends to sign the 12-month commit once legal confirms the final MA.

Best,
Sarah
